note: Re-judged 2026-10-30 by an independent auditor after the userns conversion. The unit's only change since the last verdict is userns.Enter(t) as its first statement (the child re-runs the whole body in its own user, network and mount namespace; a child failure or skip propagates to the parent, and a child that ran nothing fails it) plus removal of EPERM/EACCES skips, so a refused privilege now fails instead of skipping. Assertions are byte-identical. Section 2.0: 'Unlike other TCP extensions (e.g., the Window Scale option [RFC1323]), the absence of the option in the SYN,ACK segment must not cause the sender to disable its sending of signatures.' Single positive per the row's annotation. TestRFC2385UnsignedSYNACKDoesNotDisableSignatures dials with a key, the observer verifies the initial SYN's digest independently, injects an unsigned SYNACK acknowledging it with repaired checksums, then requires a retransmitted SYN on the same ports and sequence with an independently valid digest; the caller requires a net.Error timeout, so an unsigned establishment fails it. Observer errors return over a channel to the caller's Fatal.
